sources.entry: Scala: _A Practical Guide to Building a Cost-Based Query Planner_

summary.one_liner: A written guide, with Scala code, to building a small cost-based (Volcano-style) query planner for a tiny SQL-like SELECT/JOIN language.
keywords: learn how databases pick join order
write my own sql query optimizer
summary.what_it_does: Explains the design of a cost-based query planner, contrasting heuristic and cost-based approaches and describing the two-phase (exploration and optimization) Volcano-style lifecycle. It defines key terms such as logical and physical plans, equivalent groups, transformation and implementation rules, and the memo. The guide then builds the pieces in Scala: an AST and parser for a tiny SELECT/JOIN dialect, a logical plan with a conversion from the AST, the group/memo data structures, and initialization. It also walks through the exploration loop and two transformation rules, projection pushdown and a narrow three-table join reorder. The text is a guide with code excerpts; the full source files are referenced, not reproduced in the README.
use_cases: learn how a database query planner chooses join order
build a toy SQL parser and planner in Scala
study memo and equivalent-group data structures
implement projection pushdown as a transformation rule
notable: Walks through Volcano-style exploration and optimization with an explicit memo of equivalent groups
Includes worked Mermaid diagrams showing how the memo grows after each rule fires
Implements projection pushdown and a narrow three-table join reorder rule
Dialect is deliberately tiny: only SELECT and JOIN, with fully qualified fields
caveats: Supports only SELECT and JOIN; no filters, aggregates, or subqueries except as join sources
Join reorder is deliberately stripped down and only handles three-table joins
Exhaustive search is used for simplicity; the guide notes this is impractical in production
README is truncated; the full Scala code is in linked files not shown here
